entry.author: Wellington City Libraries
entry.summary:
The acclaimed Wellington based poet, novelist and short story writer Janis Freegard “ regarded as one of the most unique and distinctive voices in the New Zealand literary World at the moment”. Recently did a live experimental poetry reading at the  Twin Rivers Bookshop in Miramar accompanied by Librarian and soundscape artist Neil Johnstone. 
Janis is known for her works as both a poet and as a novelist, Janis Freegard moved to New Zealand when she was aged twelve and has degrees in botany, plant ecology and public management. 
She was the winner of the 2001 BNZ Katherine Mansfield Short Story Award. And was also  the winner of the 2019 Geometry/Open Book National Poetry competition.
Her work has been in numerous poetry collections and she has so far published three solo collections Kingdom Animalia: The Escapades of Linnaeus, The Continuing Adventures of Alice Spider and The Glass Rooster.
In  2014, she held the inaugural Ema Saiko Poetry Fellowship at New Pacific Studio in the Wairarapa. Which is where she commenced work on her current prose poem sequence Reading the signs which is the basis for this performance.  The finished collection took many years to complete. 
We were delighted when Janis invited us along to record this very special reading of  Reading the signs. 
We wish to extend our most heartfelt thanks to Twin Rivers Secondhand Bookshop and Janis Freegard for making this very special and totally unmissable event happen .
